notes: An 8 m tile, not 0.5 m, because Lot projects this pack in WORLD space (uv1_world_triplanar at 1/meters_per_tile) and a crosswalk bar is 0.5 m wide on a 1.0 m pitch: at 0.5 m every bar of a crosswalk sampled the same phase of the tile, and every bar repeated the same holes every 0.5 m down its 9.4 m length -- measured on cold run 9044's themed build, 36 of 36 bar pairs within a crosswalk and 84 of 210 across the site pixel-identical. The walker's question was why the paint wore in identical blotches. The colour bands keep their size in metres (every cell count x16). The wear is fbm from 4 cells (2 m) down six octaves to 6 cm, so a whole stretch of paint is worn or intact and the nicks inside it are ragged; `coverage` 0.9 keeps nine tenths of the tile at the field's own quantile, because the fixed 0.40 threshold this carried would have kept 70% at these octaves. RESIDUE THIS CANNOT REMOVE: any world-space period repeats wherever two bars stand a multiple of it apart (5 of 210 pairs on 9044 still match within 24 cm of shift at 8 m; a 7.7 m tile only moved which pairs); a per-marking uv offset in Lot is what ends that. 1024 px at 8 m is the library's 128 px/m. WET VARIANT: a paint film is not porous, so it responds like painted metal -- the least darkening of the four presets (0.30). Its cavity bias is low because a flat film has almost no recesses to pool in; the water is on it, not in it.
